summary: Bogachiel Peak lookout in Olympic NP: built 1934-35 under the NPS, Aircraft Warning station in summers from 1942, abandoned in the 1950s and reported gone; no remains described.

facts.design: L-4 14 x 14 ft ground cabin (FFLOS register says L-5)
facts.status_note: Abandoned in the 1950s and now gone, per the FFLOS register; no source describes what remains on the summit

staffing.status: Aircraft Warning Service station, summers only, from June 1942; abandoned in the 1950s

access.note: Hiking route in Olympic National Park; WTA describes a 0.3-mile side trip from the High Divide Trail to the summit

visit.trail_note: Reached from the Seven Lakes Basin or Hoh River trailheads; WTA says camping is not allowed at the summit

facts.agency: National Park Service, Olympic National Park

events.note: Forest Service bought most of the materials for a standard 14 x 14 lookout house and stored them at a Deer Lake shelter
National Park Service took over construction; crew began leveling the summit and excavating foundations September 4, 1934; work stopped October 8, 1934 for the winter
Construction resumed July 8, 1935 once the snow had cleared
Completed September 10, 1935 as a 14 x 14 L-4 ground cabin
USGS map shows the lookout and trails (photo caption on WillhiteWeb)
Activated as an Aircraft Warning Service station, summers only
A young couple spent their honeymoon at the lookout (story reprinted on WillhiteWeb)
Registered on the FFLOS January 20, 2011 as US 821

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLOS register calls it an L-5 cab. firelookout.com and the Rex's page both describe a 14 x 14 L-4 ground cabin, and WillhiteWeb says it followed the Forest Service's Standard Plan C for 14 x 14 lookout houses. The record keeps L-4 and the story notes the register's L-5.

notes_for_editor: Design is the main disagreement (FFLOS L-5 vs L-4 elsewhere). Hike length differs by source (WillhiteWeb lists 8.5 miles; WTA lists a 16.2-mile round trip for its listing); neither is a lookout fact, so neither is used. The Lookout site photo dated November 29, 2019 exists, but its caption does not describe remains and the image was not viewed. The honeymoon story is reprinted on WillhiteWeb from a book; the couple is not named in the story. No photos added.
